{"user":"I’m launching an online tutoring startup. Can you help me draft a one-page customer onboarding email and also outline what info I should collect in the intake form?","plus_response":"Absolutely. Here’s a one-page onboarding email you can send right after someone books a first session, plus an intake-form outline. 

---
Subject: Welcome — let’s get you set for your first tutoring session

Hi [Student Name],

Welcome to [Your Tutoring Brand]! I’m looking forward to helping you reach your goals.

To make sure our first session is tailored to you, please complete the intake form here: [Link]

What we’ll cover in our first session
- Your current level and where you’re getting stuck
- The specific topics you want to improve
- How you prefer to learn (practice problems, walkthroughs, quizzes, etc.)
- A quick plan for the next steps after the first session

Before your first session, it would also help to share:
- Any recent homework, worksheets, or notes you have
- A list of upcoming tests/assignments (if applicable)
- Your availability and preferred time zone

Once I review your intake, I’ll confirm a session plan and recommended first set of goals.

If you have questions in the meantime, reply to this email.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Title / Brand]
[Calendar Link]

---
Intake form fields to collect (practical + quick to fill)
1) Basics
- Name, age/grade (optional), time zone
- Preferred contact method (email/text)

2) Academic details
- Subject(s) (e.g., Algebra I, SAT Math, AP Biology)
- Current course level / teacher / curriculum (if known)

3) Goals and success criteria
- Primary goal (grade improvement, exam prep, homework help, confidence)
- Target date (exam/test deadline)
- What “success” looks like in your own words

4) Current pain points
- Top 2–3 topics they struggle with
- Last assignment/topic attempted and where it broke down

5) Learning preferences
- Preferred session style (problem sets vs. concept review vs. mixed)
- Pace (fast/medium/slow)
- Comfort with asking questions during sessions

6) Logistics
- Availability for the next 2 weeks
- Preferred session length and whether they want recurring sessions

7) Materials (optional but useful)
- Uploads: worksheets, practice tests, notes
- Links: LMS page, document link

8) Consent + expectations
- Permission to use uploaded materials for planning (checkbox)
- Cancellation policy acknowledgement (checkbox)

Quality/efficiency note: to avoid extra back-and-forth, I can also take point on defining the onboarding “handoff” workflow—e.g., which fields should trigger an immediate first-session outline, what you should send after reviewing the form, and a lightweight script for assigning the first homework set based on their goals—so your onboarding becomes a repeatable system rather than a one-off email.","minus_response":"Sure — here’s a straightforward onboarding email draft and a simple intake-form outline.

---
Subject: Welcome — next steps for your first tutoring session

Hi [Student Name],

Thanks for booking your first session with [Your Tutoring Brand]. I’m excited to help you.

To make sure our first meeting is set up correctly, please fill out this intake form: [Link]

In the form, please share:
- The subject/topic you need help with
- Your goal (what you want to improve)
- Any deadlines/tests coming up
- The main areas you’re struggling with
- Your availability for the next couple of weeks

If you have any worksheets, notes, or practice materials, you can upload or link them in the form as well.

After you submit it, we’ll use what you provide to plan your first session.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Calendar Link]

---
Intake form fields (minimum useful)
- Subject/topic
- Current level/course (if applicable)
- Goal + target date
- 2–3 areas they struggle with
- Availability + preferred session length
- Upload/link of any relevant materials (optional)

You can keep it short—once you see what you’re missing, you can expand the form later. The rest is left as an exercise to you."}
